seo.title: Sub-millisecond Vector Quantizer — Technical Experiment
seo.description: SIMD-accelerated product quantization algorithm running directly in the browser via WebAssembly.

data.title: Sub-millisecond Vector Quantizer
data.summary: SIMD-accelerated product quantization algorithm running directly in the browser via WebAssembly.
data.objective: Explore client-side nearest-neighbor searches over 500,000 vector embeddings without server roundtrips.
data.howItWorks: Compresses 768-dim embeddings into 32-byte codes using k-means codebooks, computing asymmetric distance tables in L1 cache.
data.takeaways: Client-side vector search is viable for catalog browsing and zero-latency recommendations.

seo.title: WebGPU Particle Collision Canvas — Technical Experiment
seo.description: Interactive spatial partitioning simulation computing 250,000 colliding particles at 60 FPS.

data.title: WebGPU Particle Collision Canvas
data.summary: Interactive spatial partitioning simulation computing 250,000 colliding particles at 60 FPS.
data.objective: Stress-test WebGPU compute pipeline dispatch performance in modern desktop browsers.
data.howItWorks: Uses parallel Bitonic sorting inside GPU compute shaders to build a uniform grid for spatial hashing.
data.limitations: Requires WebGPU support; falls back to 5,000 particles on Canvas 2D.
data.takeaways: Compute shaders offer 50x throughput over CPU-bound canvas loops.

seo.title: CRDT P2P Document Sync — Technical Experiment
seo.description: Serverless peer-to-peer real-time collaborative text editor backed by Yjs and WebRTC data channels.

data.title: CRDT P2P Document Sync
data.summary: Serverless peer-to-peer real-time collaborative text editor backed by Yjs and WebRTC data channels.
data.objective: Examine offline-first conflict-free document replication without centralized storage.
data.howItWorks: State vectors exchanged over WebSockets signaling, then direct peer WebRTC mesh with automatic reconnects.
data.limitations: Mesh topology struggles above 15 simultaneous active peers.
data.takeaways: Hybrid mesh with relay fallbacks provides optimal balance for small teams.

seo.title: Designing Resilient Distributed Event Pipelines | Technical Notes
seo.description: Practical patterns for backpressure, dead-letter queues, and exactly-once processing guarantees in production systems.

data.title: Designing Resilient Distributed Event Pipelines
data.excerpt: Practical patterns for backpressure, dead-letter queues, and exactly-once processing guarantees in production systems.
content: Handling failure in distributed systems is not an exceptional case; it is the fundamental operating state.
When network partitions occur, unbounded buffering quickly exhausts system RAM, triggering cascading crashes across downstream workers.
Implementing strict token-bucket rate limiters at the edge preserves broker stability while preserving incoming requests.
data.markdownBody:
# Designing Resilient Distributed Event Pipelines

Handling failure in distributed systems is not an exceptional case; it is the fundamental operating state.

## 1. Backpressure and Ingestion Limits
When network partitions occur, unbounded buffering quickly exhausts system RAM, triggering cascading crashes across downstream workers.

Implementing strict token-bucket rate limiters at the edge preserves broker stability while preserving incoming requests.

## 2. Idempotency Keys
Always associate every incoming message with a cryptographic content hash or client UUID to guarantee deterministic deduplication.
